communications.subject: Nevada Public Records Act Request: Axon Draft One Records
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Nevada Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records related to the use of any AI-assisted police report technology provided by the company Axon (previously known as Taser). This technology may be referred to as Draft One (https://www.axon.com/products/draft-one), the Axon Narrative Assistant, Axon AI, or by another name. 

For more information on the Axon Narrative Assistant, please refer to the User Guide found at this link: https://www.documentcloud.org/documents/25418151-axon-narrative-assistant-user-guide_axon-records-1-1/. 

For more information on Axon Draft One, please look at this page on the Axon website: https://www.axon.com/resources/closer-look-draft-one. 

CONTRACT AND AGREEMENTS

1.  All contracts, memorandums of understanding, and any other written agreements between this agency and Axon related to the use of Axon AI, Axon Draft One, Narrative Assistant, or any other AI-assisted report generation tool provided by Axon. 

Responsive records include all associated amendments, exhibits, and supplemental and supporting documentation. 

If access to Draft One, Axon AI or similar tools is being provided via an existing contract or through an informal agreement, please provide the relevant contract or the relevant communication or agreement that facilitated the access. This includes all agreements, both formal and informal, including all trial access, even if that access does not or did not involve financial obligations. 

2. All relevant terms of use, licensing agreements, and any other guiding materials;

TRAINING, POLICIES and USE MATERIAL

3. All training materials relevant to Draft One, Axon AI or Axon Narrative Assistant generated by this agency; 

4. All training material provided by Axon to this agency regarding its use of Draft One; 

5. All user manuals, other guidance materials, help documents, or related materials;

6. Guides, safety tests, and other supplementary material that mention Draft One provided by Axon from January 1, 2024 and the date this request is received;

7. All final reports, evaluations, reports, or other documentation concluding or summarizing a trial or evaluation period or pilot project; 

8. Any and all policies related to the use of Draft One, the Narrative Assistant, or any other AI-assisted report generation offerings provided by Axon (An example of one such policy can be found here: https://cdn.muckrock.com/foia_files/2024/11/26/608_Computer_Software_and_Transcription-Assisted_Report_Generation.pdf);


COMMUNICATIONS
9. All communications sent or received by any representative of this agency with individuals representing Axon referencing the following term, including emails and attachments: 
• Draft One
• Narrative Assistant
• AI-generated report
• Axon AI

10. All communications sent to or received by any representative of this agency with each of the following email addresses, including attachments:
a. draftone@axon.com
b. bryan@axon.com
c. noahsw@axon.com               	 
d. efleischli@axon.com (Erin Fleischli)
e. edriver@axon.com
f. eforester@axon.com (Evan Forester, Director of Product Marketing)    
g. gsigman@axon.com (Gabriel Sigman, Technical Account Manager)
h. tstuhr@axon.com (Tierney Stuhr, Sales Representative)

11. All communications sent to or received by the following representatives of this agency regarding Axon Draft One, Axon Narrative Assistant, AI-generated report or Axon AI:
a. garlocks@reno.gov (Sean Garlock, Assistant Chief of Police)

We ask that these materials be provided on a rolling basis; as your office collects and reviews records, we would appreciate it if your office would provide those materials to us incrementally. If possible, please provide any responsive contractual and financial materials within the statutorily-mandated public record law time frame. We would prefer communications to be provided next. Please contact us for further discussion regarding the search and release of these materials.

This request is not being made for commercial purposes. Please assess fees appropriately in accordance with a public records request being made in the public interest.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform us of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I request that all records be disclosed in their native, digital format and transmitted to us electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or by CD-ROM if not.

If you need any more information in order to process the request, or cannot process a portion of the request for any reason, please respond to the email address on this request or “cabrerjess@gmail.com”. Further discussion may be conducted via email. Please let us know if a phone call will be necessary or desirable; such contact information will be provided upon request.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 5 business days, as the statute requires business days.

Sincerely, 
Jesse Cabrera

To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the West Virginia Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

To the Huntington Police Department Records Custodian:

Under the West Virginia Freedom of Information Act, W. Va. Code § 29B-1-1 et seq., I request copies of the following public records about Terrance L. Taylor, a former Huntington police officer employed from about May 2000 to July 2002:

1. Records showing Taylor's dates of employment, rank or position, and date of separation.
2. Records showing the type of separation: termination, resignation or other. If Taylor was terminated, include the notice of termination and any document stating the reason.
3. Final findings and outcomes of any internal-affairs or disciplinary investigation involving Taylor, including the sanction imposed.
4. Any records of an appeal of Taylor's separation or discipline to the Huntington Police Civil Service Commission, including notices of hearing, minutes and the commission's decision.

If you withhold any part of these records under an exemption, please cite the specific exemption for each record and release the rest. Records of a public officer's employment status, discipline and separation relate to public duties, and I would ask you to weigh that.

I'm a journalist with WIRED, and these records are requested for news reporting in the public interest. I ask that any fees be waived or reduced. If fees will exceed $25, please tell me before processing. Electronic copies by email are preferred.

communications.subject: California Public Records Act Request: California Public Records Act Request — Three Strikes and Gang Enhancement Sentencing Data (2021–2026)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the California Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

This request covers the period from October 1, 2021 through October 1, 2026 and concerns individuals received by CDCR on a commitment involving one or more of the following provisions:
Penal Code § 667 (Three Strikes law, including § 667(a) five-year serious felony enhancements and § 667(b)–(i) second- and third-strike sentencing) and its companion statute, Penal Code § 1170.12
Penal Code §§ 186.20–186.36 (Street Terrorism Enforcement and Prevention Act), including the gang participation offense under § 186.22(a) and the gang enhancements and alternate penalties under § 186.22(b) and (d)
For each provision above, I request the following de-identified, record-level data (no names or CDCR numbers are requested), in electronic format such as CSV or Excel, together with the data dictionary or record layout needed to interpret it:
Date of commitment/admission, county of commitment, and sentencing court
Controlling and all other offenses of commitment, with the specific Penal Code provision for each
Each enhancement or sentencing provision applied, identified by statute (e.g., § 186.22(b)(1)(A)–(C), § 186.22(b)(4), § 186.22(d), § 667(a)(1), § 667(e)(1) second strike, § 667(e)(2) third strike, § 1170.12), with the term imposed for each
Total aggregate sentence length, and whether the term is determinate or indeterminate (e.g., 25-to-life)
Race/ethnicity, sex, and age at commitment
Current status (in custody, released, paroled, deceased, resentenced), and date of release or resentencing where applicable, including any recall or resentencing under Penal Code § 1172.1, § 1172.75, or § 1170.126

In addition, I request any existing reports, dashboards, or aggregate summaries produced by CDCR (including its periodic reports on second- and third-strike offenders in the adult institution population) that cover the same period and subject matter, as well as the data dictionary or record layout for any offender database from which the above data would be drawn.
Please note that Penal Code § 186.22 was substantially amended by Assembly Bill 333, effective January 1, 2022. If feasible, I ask that the data distinguish commitments imposed before and after that date.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 calendar days, as the statute requires.

title: Police PROTECT Act Compliance Sept-Oct 2026

communications.subject: Massachusetts Public Records Law Request: Police PROTECT Act Compliance Sept-Oct 2026
communications.communication:
Dear Record Access Officer:

This is a request under the Massachusetts Public Records Law (M. G. L. Chapter 66, Section 10). I am requesting the following records:

1.    All police department policies SOPs or other records currently in effect regarding communication and information sharing between departmental employees and federal agents/agencies within the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) or the U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS), including but not limited to the U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). The records request includes, but is not limited to, policies regarding:

             A. Fingerprint and other data sharing;
             B. Compliance with federal immigration enforcement efforts, including guidance or policies concerning when communication with ICE officers is allowed. This includes how and under what circumstances to respond to ICE detainer requests or when and how department employees can provide a federal immigration authority with nonpublic personal information, custody status, or advance notice of a person’s release from pretrial detention or upcoming court appearances;
             C. Any other records that indicate changes in policy, practice, or training as a result of the passage of the Massachusetts PROTECT Act in August 2026.

 2.  All departmental policies, guidance, memos or other records concerning the use of local resources for federal civil immigration enforcement. This includes policies, requests or responses to requests for the use of state police parking lots, police station/barracks interior or exterior areas for immigration enforcement, staging, or the transfer of custody.

3.    Any records of email, text, or phone conversations between department employees and federal DHS employees working at ICE made from September 4, 2026 until October 31, 2026, including but not limited to email sent to any “@ice.dhs.gov” email address. This request includes any call logs or transcripts of calls.

For each request, I am not seeking identifying information of community members, and I will accept anonymized or redacted data as necessary to protect the identity of the public. Redaction of names of municipal, state, or federal government employees is not necessary.

Pursuant to 950 CMR 32.07(2)(k), I request that your agency waive fees given that these records are in the public interest and I am not requesting this for commercial interests. Mr. LaRussa was a restaurateur and associate of the Bruno crime family in Philadelphia. He was born in Campo dell Gatto, Italy, to Giuseppe (Joseph) LaRussa and Marianna LaRussa in 1938 and moved to the United States in 1951. A decade later, he began running so-called bust-out bars for the Bruno crime family in Philadelphia's red-light district on Locust Street, including the Bag o' Nails and HMS Pinafore; these were Mob-run dives that offered nude dancers and prostitution. The businesses provided Mr. LaRussa with enough capital to open a restaurant, La Cucina, that quickly became a hangout for Nicodemo "Little Nicky" Scarfo, successor to Bruno family boss Angelo Bruno.
